patterns.usage_note: Casual spoken contraction of としても (〜たって is the colloquial counterpart of 〜ても); it grants a supposition for the sake of argument, and the second clause typically brushes it aside as making no difference. Both take plain forms, but にしたって leans on nouns naming a real person or case, while としたって leans on a supposition — その噂が事実だとしたって (hypothetical) vs 部長にしたって (real case in point). Polite としましても is the same expression at higher register; としたところで is close but adds ところで's sense that the supposition would change nothing.

examples.ruby: いくら安[やす]いとしたって、三[みっ]つも買[か]うのは多[おお]すぎる。
examples.english: Even supposing they're cheap, buying three of them is too many.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]晴[は]れるとしたって、この風[かぜ]では船[ふね]は出[で]ないよ。
examples.english: Even supposing it clears up tomorrow, the boats won't go out in this wind.

examples.ruby: その噂[うわさ]が事実[じじつ]だとしたって、私[わたし]は驚[おどろ]かない。
examples.english: Even assuming that rumor is true, it wouldn't surprise me.

glosses: even; even in the case of
patterns.usage_note: Casual spoken contraction of にしても that most often names something real and grants it as an extreme or representative case (部長にしたって "even the boss, for his part"); with a plain verb it also works hypothetically, like にしても, and the following clause is usually negative or deflating. Polite にしましても is the same expression at higher register; にしたところで adds the sense that it would make no difference.

examples.ruby: 部長[ぶちょう]にしたって、この状況[じょうきょう]は予想外[よそうがい]だっただろう。
examples.english: Even the boss can't have seen this situation coming.

examples.ruby: 手伝[てつだ]うにしたって、道具[どうぐ]がなければ何[なに]もできない。
examples.english: Even if I pitch in, there's nothing I can do without the tools.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]や二度[にど]失敗[しっぱい]したにしたって、諦[あきら]める必要[ひつよう]はないよ。
examples.english: So you slip up once or twice — that's no reason to give up.

glosses: no matter how much … , it's no use
patterns.usage_note: Attaches to the ta-form (だとこで・だところで after the voiced sound changes of 五段 ガ・ナ・バ・マ行 verbs): the speaker frames the action as unrealized and futile, so the second clause carries a negative or a judgment like 無駄だ・意味がない rather than reporting a past fact. Unlike ものの, which concedes something that actually happened, たところで supposes an action that would change nothing, and it is cooler and more dismissive than ても. とこで is a very casual clip of ところで; the same clip also serves the unrelated temporal ところで ("just as …"), so the futility reading depends on a negative or dismissive second clause.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]から急[いそ]いだとこで、終電[しゅうでん]には間[ま]に合[あ]わないよ。
examples.english: Hurrying now isn't going to get us on the last train.

examples.ruby: どれだけ悩[なや]んだとこで、答[こた]えなんて出[で]てこないよ。
examples.english: No matter how long you agonize over it, no answer is going to come.

examples.ruby: 今更[いまさら]練習[れんしゅう]したところで、優勝[ゆうしょう]には届[とど]かないよ。
examples.english: Practicing at this point isn't going to get us to the championship.

patterns.usage_note: Concessive 「even if / whether or not」 that often signals the speaker's insistence that the main point stands regardless; it is commonly doubled as 〜にしろ〜にしろ to list alternatives, and it contrasts with にしたって, which grants one real case and deflates it. On the formality scale it sits between the stiffer, more written にせよ and the softer conversational にしても. Note that な-adjectives and nouns also take である before it in careful writing, and that the form is identical to the imperative of にする, so context decides.

examples.ruby: 冗談[じょうだん]にしろ、言[い]っていいことと悪[わる]いことがある。
examples.english: Even as a joke, there are things you say and things you don't.

examples.ruby: 参加[さんか]するにしろ、事前[じぜん]に連絡[れんらく]だけはしてほしい。
examples.english: Even if you do take part, I'd like you to let us know beforehand.

examples.ruby: 以前[いぜん]断[ことわ]られたにしろ、頼[たの]み直[なお]す価値[かち]はあると思[おも]う。
examples.english: Granted they turned us down before, I still think it's worth asking again.
